title: A Hybrid Quantum–Classical Variational Linear Solver for Power Flow Analysis in Smart Grids with V2G Integration
content: Power flow analysis is essential for evaluating the steady-state operation of modern smart grids, particularly when distributed energy resources and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) systems are integrated into distribution networks. This study presents a hybrid quantum–classical framework that combines a Variational Quantum Linear Solver (VQLS) with the COBYLA optimizer for AC power flow analysis. The nonlinear power flow equations are linearized iteratively, and the resulting Jacobian-based linear system is approximated using a parameterized quantum circuit. The framework is evaluated using a modified IEEE 33-bus radial distribution system with an aggregated V2G unit connected at Bus 18. In the main optimization run, the VQLS cost decreases rapidly and approaches a stable nonzero value, while the resulting bus-voltage profile follows the overall trend of the Newton–Raphson reference solution. A separate 50-iteration convergence assessment also shows a substantial cost reduction, although the prescribed tolerance of 10−4 is not reached. The V2G scenario analysis indicates that active power losses during the evening peak are reduced as V2G participation increases, with the 50% smart-discharge case producing the lowest losses among the investigated conditions. In addition, a resource-scaling assessment for systems ranging from 14 to 300 buses shows different growth trends between the normalized classical computation index and the VQLS circuit-depth index. These results support the numerical feasibility of integrating a VQLS-based approximation into iterative power flow analysis. The study remains a simulation-based proof of concept and does not claim computational superiority or quantum speedup over established classical solvers.
